title: Binary search for 45 in a sorted array of eight values
determinism: no randomness; the input is fixed
notes: The linear-scan comparison count is computed from the same array, so the 'O(n) versus O(log n)' claim in the summary is measured rather than asserted.

steps.label: Step 1: the window is indices 0 to 7 (8 values); the midpoint index 3 holds 25, below the target 45, so the left half is discarded and the window becomes 4 to 7.
Step 2: the window is indices 4 to 7 (4 values); the midpoint index 5 holds 45, which is the target. Found after 2 comparisons.

alt.first: Binary search starts with the whole array of 8 values in play and tests the midpoint against the target 45.
alt.last: Binary search found 45 in 2 comparisons; the linear scan needed 6 on the same array. The window halves every step, so the cost is log base 2 of n — but only because the array was sorted first.
